1.title: Cloud Migration and Compute Terms
1.text: Welcome to Module eight: Cloud Migration and Compute Terms. It covers the exam area All categories. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Migration terms. Compute terms. How compute options compare. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: four. Modernize infrastructure and applications with Google Cloud (about eighteen percent). Exam format: ninety minutes and fifty to sixty multiple-choice questions. Validated against: the official Google Cloud Digital Leader exam guide.

1.title: Migration terms
1.text: Migration terms. A workload is an application or task and the resources it uses. Each workload may take a different path.

1.title: Migration terms, continued
1.text: Migration terms. The figure shows this: The migration paths from retire and retain to rehost, replatform, refactor and reimagine.

1.title: Migration terms, continued
1.text: Migration terms. Discovery and assessment. Meaning: Inventory workloads and decide the path for each. Effort and benefit: First step. Retire. Meaning: Switch off an application that is no longer needed. Effort and benefit: Saves cost. Retain. Meaning: Keep it where it is, for now. Effort and benefit: No change, revisit later. Rehost (lift and shift). Meaning: Move as is to virtual machines in the cloud. Effort and benefit: Fast, low effort, few cloud benefits.

1.title: Migration terms, continued
1.text: Migration terms. Replatform (move and improve). Meaning: Move with small changes to use managed services (for example a managed database). Effort and benefit: Moderate effort, better operations. Refactor. Meaning: Change the code to be cloud-native (for example microservices). Effort and benefit: High effort, high benefit. Reimagine. Meaning: Rebuild or replace the application to create new business value (new product, A I). Effort and benefit: Highest effort and innovation. Exam tip: Rehost equals fastest. Refactor and reimagine equals most benefit, most effort. Rehost fits specialized legacy apps you cannot change.

1.title: Compute terms
1.text: Compute terms. Virtual machine. A computer simulated in software, with its own operating system. Containerization and containers. Packaging an app with what it needs to run the same way anywhere; lighter than V Ms. Microservices. An app built from small, independent services that scale and update separately. Serverless computing. You run code or containers without managing servers; pay per use; scales to zero. Spot V Ms. Discounted V Ms that Google can stop when it needs the capacity; for flexible, fault-tolerant jobs.

1.title: Compute terms, continued
1.text: Compute terms. Kubernetes. Open source system to run and manage containers at scale. Autoscaling. Add or remove capacity automatically with demand. Load balancing. Spread traffic across several servers. Managed services. Google runs the operations (patching, scaling, backups) so your team builds instead of operates. Exam tip: Spot V Ms are cheap but can be interrupted, so use them for batch and fault-tolerant work, not for a critical single server.

1.title: How compute options compare
1.text: How compute options compare. Virtual machines. Control: Most. Management effort: Highest. Containers on Kubernetes. Control: High. Management effort: Medium. Serverless. Control: Least. Management effort: Lowest. Exam tip: Match the path to the goal: speed equals rehost, managed services with small change equals replatform, cloud-native benefits equals refactor, new business value equals reimagine, no longer needed equals retire.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A company wants to move a specialized legacy application to the cloud quickly without changing the code. Which migration path fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Rehost, which moves it as it is. Rehost, or lift and shift, moves the application as it is, which is fast and needs no code change.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A company keeps its database but moves it to a managed database service to cut operations work, with small changes. Which path is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Replatform, which makes small changes to use managed services. Replatform, or move and improve, adopts managed services with small changes.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. An application is no longer used by anyone. What should the assessment recommend? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Retire it to save cost. An unused application should be retired.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which step should come first in a migration program? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Discovery and assessment of the workloads. Discovery and assessment inventories workloads and chooses a path for each.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A company runs nightly batch jobs that can restart if interrupted and wants the lowest compute cost. Which option fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Spot V Ms, discounted capacity that can be stopped. Spot V Ms are discounted and fit fault-tolerant, restartable work.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which technology lets a team run code without managing servers and pay only when it runs? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Serverless computing. Serverless computing removes server management and charges per use.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does rehost mean? Answer: Move an application as it is (lift and shift). Question two. What does refactor mean? Answer: Change the code to be cloud-native. Question three. What is a container? Answer: An app packaged with what it needs to run anywhere.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is Kubernetes? Answer: An open source system for running containers at scale. Question five. What is a spot V M? Answer: A discounted V M that can be stopped when Google needs capacity. Question six. What does autoscaling do? Answer: Adds or removes capacity automatically.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Paths: assess, retire, retain, rehost, replatform, refactor, reimagine. Effort: rehost least; refactor and reimagine most; benefit rises with effort. Compute: V M, container, microservice, serverless, Kubernetes. Cost and scale: spot V Ms cheap but interruptible; autoscaling; load balancing.
